newsitem.title: GERMANY: Thyssen urges no reaction from shareholders. [CORRECTED 18:43 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Thyssen urges no reaction from shareholders. [CORRECTED 18:43 GMT]

text.p: German steel and engineering group Thyssen AG on Tuesday recommended shareholders not react initially to a cash offer by its smaller rival Krupp.
In a statement, Thyssen said it would thoroughly review the offer from Fried. Krupp AG Hoesch-Krupp, but that it saw no need to negotiate with Krupp.
Thyssen urges shareholders to stand pat
"The Thyssen board reacted to the announcement of a cash offer by Krupp for Thyssen shares with the recommendation to shareholders to remain calm and do nothing," Thyssen said in a statement.

"Thyssen, advised by Credit Suisse First Boston, Morgan Stanley, J.P. Morgan and SBC Warburg, sees no need to negotiate. It will thoroughly review the offer and express a well-based opinion to shareholders shortly," it said.
Krupp offered Thyssen shareholders 435 marks a share, a 25 percent premium on Monday's closing share price. Analysts valued the total offer at 13.6 billion marks.
